synthesis: The bound parents do not establish one exact 1/log T threshold across all three representations: the matrix transition is organized by N|alpha|, the lower-bound contour groups poles at distance O(1/log T), but the prime-sum lemma changes behavior at |a| comparable to 1/log z.
source_support: Units u01, u05, and u06 connect N with log(T/2pi) and distinguish coalesced, finite, and separated matrix shifts through N|alpha|; u11 and u12 encode zeta-shift differences as pole locations and enclose the microscopic poles in a circle of radius c/log T. In contrast, u09 proves only a bound by log min(1/|a|,log z), whose crossover is 1/log z.
nonparaphrase_operation: Comparing the scale variables across the three representations exposes a failed identification: N maps to log(T/2pi) in the random-matrix model and the resonator contour is chosen at c/log T, whereas the prime polynomial retains its independent truncation parameter z.
limits: The prime-sum parent neither identifies log z with log T nor supplies the later upper-bound specialization that could convert its cutoff. The matching matrix and contour orders also do not prove conjectured zeta asymptotic constants.
quality_reason: Rejected because the central simultaneous-threshold claim replaces the formula-sensitive prime cutoff 1/log z by 1/log T without support from the assigned parents. The relation is concrete for the matrix and lower-bound contour units, but the third required representation is not established; there is no source corruption warranting quarantine.

synthesis: The upper and lower bounds reach the same shift-dependent pairwise factor through different interfaces. The upper route logarithmizes the zeta product, controls weighted log-zeta level sets through a prime-polynomial covariance parameter W, and recovers the moment by layer-cake integration. The lower route correlates a smoothed coefficient expansion of the zeta product with a short resonator, uses Fourier localization to retain its diagonal, and evaluates that resonator norm through an Euler product and clustered residues.
source_support: Unit u07 writes the moment as an integral over level-set measures and defines W as a sum of diagonal log log T terms and pairwise log min(1/|alpha_i-alpha_j|,log T) terms; u08 and u10 reduce those tails to moment bounds for prime blocks. On the lower side, u13 supplies the smoothed Dirichlet expansion, u14 reduces the correlation integral to the positive diagonal, and u11 evaluates the surviving norm with the product over min(1/|alpha_i-alpha_j|,log T) raised to 2k_i k_j.
nonparaphrase_operation: The upper route transforms a multiplicative moment into an additive deviation variable whose covariance sum W is exponentiated by tail integration; the lower route transforms the same zeta product into coefficients, projects onto the diagonal by the Fourier kernel, and turns that diagonal norm into the multiplicative pairwise scale via Perron/Euler-product singularities.
limits: The upper tail route is RH-conditional and its cutoffs depend on the displayed deviation regimes. The lower route is unconditional only under its positive-integer exponents, shift bounds including |alpha_i|=O(log log T), beta control, smoothing, and resonator-length conditions, and it yields a lower bound rather than an asymptotic. Equality of the resulting order does not identify constants or make either interface interchangeable.
quality_reason: Accepted because several distinct parent units jointly establish both transformations and their convergence on the same explicit pairwise product; no single parent contains the upper/lower duality. The synthesis preserves the different hypotheses and proof outputs rather than treating a shared theme as a causal explanation.

synthesis: The source handles coalescence by combining singular contributions before evaluating the limit. In the matrix model, a joint characteristic-polynomial moment becomes an ordinary moment of order 2k when N|alpha| tends to zero, while at finite scaled separation the apparently singular determinant/Vandermonde quotient has a confluent finite extension. In the zeta lower-bound norm, zero and all microscopic shifted poles are enclosed by one contour so their collective Laurent/Taylor contribution can be estimated without assigning unstable separate residues.
source_support: Unit u04 rescales the matrix contour variables and shows that merging the zero and shifted pole sets recovers the ordinary 2k moment. Unit u06 states the finite-scale determinant divided by a squared Vandermonde and requires continuous extension at collisions; u15 proves that extension by successive row and column divided differences, extracting the matching squared Vandermonde. Unit u12 separately groups the zero and O(1/log T) zeta poles inside one circle and shows that the collective leading term has the required close/far product scale.
nonparaphrase_operation: Divided differences turn numerator antisymmetry into explicit Vandermonde divisibility and a confluent derivative determinant, whereas the clustered zeta contour turns several close residues into one local coefficient extraction. These are distinct repairs implementing the same order-of-operations principle: group first, then take the collision limit or leading contribution.
limits: This is a mechanism-level analogy within the source, not an identity between the matrix transition constant and the zeta residue constant. The divided-difference argument proves existence, not positivity or a closed form; the clustered zeta calculation is tailored to the resonator norm and bounded scaled differences. The higher 2k moment conclusion belongs to complete coalescence in the matrix model, not to every clustered zeta configuration.
quality_reason: Accepted because u04, u06, and u15 establish the matrix coalescence and removable-singularity mechanism, while the distinct u12 calculation supplies a concrete contour analogue. Their conjunction adds a precise representation-level relation unavailable from either side alone and states rather than hides the mismatch between the two constants.
